probes.question: Hello, I'm Dr. Patel, one of the emergency doctors on tonight. What brought you in?
probes.target: You were fine until about 10 o'clock last night, when a sharp pain in your upper stomach came on suddenly.
probes.credits: Introduced yourself by name and role

probes.question: Can you walk me through what happened from the moment it began until you got here?
probes.target: If the doctor asks you to tell them more, say "It started around 10 last night. I took some antacids but they didn't help. It got so bad I threw up. I couldn't sleep. I finally told my husband I couldn't stand it any longer and we came here."

probes.question: Could you point to the spot where it's hurting most?
probes.target: The pain is "mostly right here". You slowly point to the upper middle of your stomach, just below the breastbone. "But now it hurts all over."

probes.question: Has it moved around at all since it began, or stayed in one place?
probes.target: The pain was always in the same place. Say "It was always just right here."

probes.question: What does the pain feel like to you?
probes.target: The pain is stabbing. Say "It's sharp and hurts all the time."

probes.question: Is it there all the time, or does it let up now and then?
probes.target: The pain is constant. Say "It never goes away."

probes.question: If zero is no pain and ten is the worst you can imagine, where is it right now?
probes.target: The pain is severe. On a scale of 1 to 10 it is a 10.

probes.question: Does the pain spread anywhere else, like round to your back?
probes.target: The pain also goes to the middle of your back, "like a knife in my gut".

probes.question: Have you found anything that makes it feel better?
probes.target: What makes it better? "Nothing makes it better."
probes.credits: What makes it better or worse

probes.question: Is there a way of lying that takes the edge off it even a bit?
probes.target: If asked whether anything lessens it, or whether any position helps, say "If I don't move at all, it helps a little. The antacids didn't help at all." Lying still helps a little.
probes.credits: What makes it better or worse

probes.question: Does anything make it hurt more?
probes.target: What makes it worse? "If I move or take a deep breath it gets worse."
probes.credits: What makes it better or worse

probes.question: Did you try taking anything for it before coming in?
probes.target: If asked what medicines you have tried, say "I tried taking 2 TUMS last night, but they didn't help."

probes.question: Have you actually been sick, thrown up at all?
probes.target: You vomited once, in the middle of the night, around midnight.

probes.question: What did it look like when it came up?
probes.target: The vomit was last night's dinner, greenish yellow. There was not a lot of food in it.

probes.question: Was there any blood in it, or anything dark that looked like coffee grounds?
probes.target: There was no blood in the vomit and nothing like coffee grounds.

probes.question: When did you last have something to eat, and what was it?
probes.target: Your last meal was dinner last night, around 6 pm, right after you came home from work. Leftover pork chops, spicy cabbage and iced tea.

probes.question: Have you been feeling hot, or getting the shivers?
probes.target: You don't know if you had a fever, but you feel cold and sweaty right now. Say "I feel like I have a fever right now."

probes.question: When you last went to the toilet for a poo, what colour was it?
probes.target: Your stools are brown. No blood and no black stools. Say "My stools are brown. I didn't see any blood."

probes.question: And your pee, has that looked normal, no blood?
probes.target: Your urine was yellow, with no blood.

probes.question: Have you ever had a pain like this in the past?
probes.target: You have never had stomach pain like this before.

probes.question: Do you see a doctor for any long-term health problems?
probes.target: You are treated for high blood pressure and high cholesterol. You see your family doctor every year for a checkup. She often tells you to quit smoking, but it has been very hard.

probes.question: Are you on any regular tablets from your doctor?
probes.target: Prescription medicines: "Yes, I take three different pills for my blood pressure and cholesterol: metoprolol, Benicar and simvastatin."

probes.question: What about things you buy yourself at the pharmacy, like painkillers for headaches?
probes.target: You take Motrin or aspirin now and then for headaches. Most recently you took 3 Motrin two days ago.

probes.question: Do you use any recreational drugs?
probes.target: You take no street drugs.

probes.question: Have you ever stayed in hospital or had an operation?
probes.target: You were in hospital for a tonsillectomy when you were 10.

probes.question: When was your last period, and any bleeding since?
probes.target: You have had no periods for 10 years. No spotting. Your Pap test is normal every year. All your pregnancies and deliveries were vaginal and normal.

probes.question: Are you sexually active, and with one partner?
probes.target: You have been in a monogamous relationship with your husband for 35 years, and you have always enjoyed a good sex life.

probes.question: Do you smoke at all?
probes.target: You smoke a pack of Marlboros a day, and have for 45 years. You know you should quit, but you could not quit with the patch.

probes.question: How much beer, wine or spirits do you usually have in a day?
probes.target: Alcohol: you call yourself a social drinker. Give the amount only if the doctor asks how much you drink: you usually have one or two beers every day, and sometimes more, depending on the social occasion. You don't get drunk and you have never been arrested for drunk driving.

probes.question: Have you ever felt you should drink less, or has anyone complained about it?
probes.target: You have never thought about cutting down. Nobody gets angry about your drinking. You don't feel guilty about it. You never need a drink in the morning to get going.

probes.question: How much coffee or fizzy drinks do you get through in a day?
probes.target: You drink at least two cups of coffee a day, one in the morning and one about 10 am, and at least two diet Cokes, one at lunch and one about 3 pm.

probes.question: What do you normally eat in a day, and do you get much exercise?
probes.target: You usually skip breakfast, have a sandwich for lunch, and "meat and potatoes" for dinner. You do not exercise regularly.

probes.question: What do you like doing in your free time?
probes.target: Hobbies and activities: you are in too much pain to talk about that.

probes.question: What kind of work do you do, and how long have you been at it?
probes.target: You have driven for one trucking company for the past 30 years. You are thinking about retiring in the next few years. You finished high school.

probes.question: Who's at home with you? Any kids?
probes.target: You have been married for 35 years. Your husband works at Walmart. You have three children, all grown and in good health.

probes.question: Do any illnesses run in your family, parents or brothers and sisters?
probes.target: Your father died of a heart attack at 55. Your mother died recently at 82 from a stroke. Your brother is 62 and has coronary artery disease.

probes.question: Have you noticed your skin or the whites of your eyes going yellow?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: Have you had any runny, watery bowel movements?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: Have you been abroad or travelled anywhere unusual lately?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: Are you allergic to any medicines?
probes.target: NOT IN CASE

probes.question: I'm going to press gently on your tummy now. Say if it's too much and I'll stop.
probes.target: It hurts all over your stomach, but it is worst in the center, just below the breastbone.
probes.credits: Checked on comfort during the exam

probes.question: We'll also need to do an internal check of your back passage and a pelvic exam as part of looking into this.
probes.target: OPEN
probes.credits: Mentioned the need for a rectal or pelvic exam

probes.question: I think there may be a hole in the lining of your stomach from an ulcer. We'll do blood tests and an x-ray and scan, and I'll get the surgeons to see you. How do you feel about that?
probes.target: You are worried about the possibility of having an operation.
probes.credits: Explained what is going on and what next

probes.question: Is there anything else going on that I haven't asked about?
probes.target: OPEN

probes.question: Anything else you'd like me to know before we get things moving?
probes.target: OPEN
